answer: Timber-linked invocation quotas. Each agent gets a unique, hardware-rooted key whose issuance requires solving a rotating computational puzzle seeded by a public "timber" beacon—a slow, memory-hard chain that cannot be parallelized cheaply. Agents may only invoke the network by spending quota derived from their key's age and a local "echo" of past puzzle solutions; every action emits a "ripple" that consumes quota and updates neighbors' difficulty.
